article_title: UK will have 'voice' but no vote on EU food rules in Brexit reset

tasks.prompt: What is the central trade-off in the proposed UK-EU food deal?
options: The UK would stop exporting food but gain control of EU elections
The UK would reduce trade barriers by aligning with EU rules while lacking a vote on those rules
The EU would adopt every British food regulation
The UK would leave all European trade arrangements immediately
tasks.correct_answer: The UK would reduce trade barriers by aligning with EU rules while lacking a vote on those rules
tasks.explanation_hebrew: העסקה אמורה לצמצם חסמי סחר באמצעות התאמה לכללי האיחוד, אך לבריטניה לא תהיה זכות הצבעה על הכללים.

tasks.prompt: Why might the agreement include an exit clause?
options: To allow supermarkets to stop selling imported food
Because the EU worries a future UK government could reverse the alignment and force border facilities to be rebuilt
To ban Conservative and Reform politicians from future summits
Because the deal requires an immediate membership fee
tasks.correct_answer: Because the EU worries a future UK government could reverse the alignment and force border facilities to be rebuilt
tasks.explanation_hebrew: האיחוד חושש שממשלה עתידית תבטל את ההסדרים, ואז יהיה צורך לבנות מחדש מתקני בדיקות גבול שיפורקו.

tasks.prompt: How much documentation can some M&S food-export trucks require?
options: Fewer than ten pages
About 30 pages
More than 300 pages
No paperwork at all
tasks.explanation_hebrew: לפי הכתבה, חלק ממשאיות היצוא של M&S זקוקות ליותר מ־300 עמודי מסמכים.

tasks.prompt: What does “rule taker” mean in the criticism of the reset?
options: A country that follows rules it cannot formally vote on
A government that writes every EU regulation
A firm that refuses to export food
A shopper who compares supermarket prices
tasks.correct_answer: A country that follows rules it cannot formally vote on
tasks.explanation_hebrew: rule taker הוא צד שמקבל ומיישם כללים שנקבעים במקום אחר, בלי כוח הצבעה פורמלי עליהם.

tasks.prompt: What economic effect is calculated for the wider agreement?
options: A fall of 5% in UK GDP
No measurable economic change
An addition of 0.4% to UK GDP
A doubling of all food prices
tasks.correct_answer: An addition of 0.4% to UK GDP
tasks.explanation_hebrew: ההסכם הרחב, הכולל גם מסחר בפליטות ותוכנית ניידות לצעירים, מוערך כתוספת של 0.4% לתמ״ג.

tasks.prompt: What are “carve-outs” in the NFU's comments?
options: Special exceptions from parts of the general rules
Physical inspections of farm buildings
Cuts to supermarket shelves
New varieties of gene-edited tomatoes
tasks.correct_answer: Special exceptions from parts of the general rules
tasks.explanation_hebrew: carve-outs הם חריגים או פטורים מיוחדים המאפשרים לתחומים מסוימים לא להיות כפופים לכלל במלואו.

tasks.prompt: Why does Falconer argue that alignment could reduce food prices?
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לתאר את שרשרת ההשפעה מניירת ובדיקות ועד למחיר לצרכן.
expected_points: Current exporters face extensive forms, certificates and border checks
Errors can cause delays or rejection
Reduced paperwork and inspections would lower firms' trading costs
Lower import and export costs could reduce supermarket costs
Falconer hopes those savings would reach shoppers

tasks.prompt: Summarise the expected benefits and main criticisms of the Brexit reset for food trade.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להציג יתרונות מסחריים וכלכליים לצד אובדן שליטה וחששות חקלאיים.
expected_points: It could reduce inspections, paperwork, delays and barriers to exports
It may lower costs and potentially prices
The food element is said to add £5bn and the wider deal 0.4% to GDP
Critics say the UK would follow rules without a vote
Farmers want details on exceptions and transition arrangements
Pesticides, precision breeding and some ingredients remain contentious

tasks.prompt: Why does the report use smoky bacon crisps as an example in the debate?
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להסביר כיצד הדוגמה ממחישה גם חשש ציבורי וגם התאמה עסקית שכבר מתרחשת.
expected_points: There were claims that stricter EU ingredient rules could restrict popular flavours
Falconer used the example to challenge what he called misinformation
Leading snack brands have already changed recipes to meet EU rules
Exporters often align with their largest market even without a formal reset
The example makes an abstract regulatory debate concrete for consumers

tasks.prompt: Write a balanced paragraph assessing whether reduced trade friction justifies accepting EU food rules without a UK vote.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להציג תועלת ועלות דמוקרטית או רגולטורית, ולהשתמש בעובדות מהכתבה.
expected_points: Benefits include less paperwork, fewer border checks and potentially lower prices
Food exports to the EU have fallen by more than a third since 2019
The UK would have some influence in shaping rules but no formal vote
Future rules could affect pesticides, gene editing or ingredients
A reasoned conclusion should weigh economic gains against reduced regulatory control
